full_judgment:
Md. Muzammel Hossain J. Delay of 535 days in filing the leave petition is condoned. This petition for leave to appeal under Article 103 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh is directed against the judgment and decree dated 17.07.2001 (decree signed on 28.11.2011) passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 134 of 1991 allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree dated 31.12.1988 (decree signed on 05.01.1989) passed by the learned Subordinate Judge (presently Joint District Judge), Bagerhat in Title Suit No. 93 of 1982 decreeing the suit. 

 5. After considering the evidence on record, the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, Bagerhat by the judgment and decree dated 31.12.1988 (decree signed on 05.01.1989) decreed the suit in full declaring that all the impugned registered deeds were fraudulent, void, collusive, illegal and not binding upon the plaintiff. 

 6. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree dated 31.12.1988 the defendants preferred an appeal being First Appeal No. 134 of 1991 before the High Court Division. A Division Bench of the High Court Division by the impugned judgment and decree date 17.07.2011 allowed the appeal in the absence of the appellant and the respondent upon reversing   the judgment and decree passed by the Trial Court. 

 7. Thereafter, the petitioners being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and decree passed by the High Court Division preferred the instant Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal before this Division. 

 8. Mr. Golam Mohiuddin, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-petitioner submits that the High Court Division committed error of law in misreading the evidence on record and filed to consider the admitted facts and in basing decision on mere surmises and conjectures and as such the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside. He submits that the High Court Division has misread, misconstrued and misunderstood the materials on record and consequently failed to comprehend the facts of the case. He then submits that the impugned judgment and decree has not been passed by the High Court Division in accordance with law rather it has been passed in violation of the mandatory provisions of law pursuant to Order 41 rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure. He finally submits that the High Court Division committed error of law by misreading, misappreciating and non-considering the evidence on record and as such the impugned judgment and decree passed by the High Court Division is liable to be aside. 

 "It is to be noticed that this rule (rule 30) does not make it incumbent on the appellate Court to refer to any part of the proceedings in the court from whose decree the appeal is preferred. The appellate Court can refer after hearing the parties and their pleaders, to any part of these proceeding to which reference be considered necessary. It is in the discretion of the appellate Court to refer to the proceedings. It is competent to pronounce judgment after hearing what the parties or their pleaders submit to it for consideration. It follows therefore   that if the appellant submits nothing for its consideration, the appellate Court can decide the appeal without any reference to any proceedings of the Courts below and, in doing so, it can simply say that the appellants have not urged anything which would tend to show that the judgment and decree under appeal were wrong." 

 "Rule 30, Judgment when and where pronounced. The Appellate Court, after hearing the parties or their pleaders and referring to any part of the proceedings, whether on appeal or in the court from whose decree the appeal is preferred, to which reference may be considered necessary, shall pronounce judgment in open Court, either at once or on some future day of which notice shall be given to the parties or their pleaders."
